1.Sub-event_summary: VII Corps ordered 31 August to turn north through Avesnes, Maubeuge, Mons, addressing gap with Third Army using reinforced 4th Cavalry Group, aiming for Meuse bridgehead near Mézières. Swerved 3d Armored from Sedan-Charleville to Hirson-Vervins, with 9th Division protecting flank, 1st reinforcing. 3d Armored reached near Mons by 2 September nightfall, columns stretched to Avesnes. Hodges unable to halt due to communication, took Mons morning 3 September. 9th at Charleroi, 1st pushing to Avesnes.

1.Sub-event_summary: On 3 September, First Army reoriented eastward, with V Corps moving across VII Corps to the right, XIX and VII advancing left and center. V Corps, filling gap with Third Army, advanced through Ardennes, crossing Meuse by 5 September, facing minimal resistance. Spread thin, units moved in columns, shifting for main effort toward Pruem and Koblenz. By 8 September, planned West Wall attack; 5th Armored entered Luxembourg on 10 September, liberating capital unopposed. Gerow ordered assembly on St. Vith-Echternach line to probe West Wall, but Hodges postponed attack for ammunition, marking pursuit's end.

French Resistance leaders in Paris sought external aid amid concerns of disorder and political upheaval, leading to canceled plans for arms airdrops, reaffirmation of using the 2d French Armored Division for liberation, de Gaulle's pressure on Eisenhower, and Leclerc's unauthorized dispatch of a reconnaissance force under Guillebon toward Paris on 21 August 1944, prompting disciplinary action from Gerow and Leclerc's appeal to higher command.

2.Sub-event_summary: On evening of 3 September, VII Corps deployed from Mons to south of Charleroi. 9th Division ordered to seize Meuse bridgehead near Dinant, faced roadblocks and strong defense, establishing bridgeheads but facing counterattacks until relieved by 3d Armored task force on 6 September, taking Dinant on 7 September. 3d Armored, delayed by gasoline at Mons, advanced to Namur by 6 September, then to Huy and Liège by 7 September, mopping up with local welcome. Advanced on Liège-Aachen axis, taking Verviers and Eupen on 9 and 11 September, noting increasing resistance and sullen populace. By end of 10 September, deployed along Malmédy-Verviers-Herve, losing contact as Germans withdrew to West Wall, ending pursuit.

3.Sub-event_summary: Dempsey's Second British Army advanced spectacularly, crossing Somme on 31 August and 1 September, capturing Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent by 3-5 September, reaching Albert Canal. Crerar's First Canadian Army took ports like Dieppe, invested others, crossed Somme on 2 September, reached Belgian-Dutch border by mid-September, overran V-weapon sites by 6 September.
